title: tramlines markdown schema
description: What a schema can state about the documents that it governs. A schema is strict by default: whatever it declares is required, whatever it doesn't declare is rejected, and each requirement is exclusive. You relax a rule only with a key that you write on purpose. A key that ends in `-open` opens a set that is otherwise rejected, and `optional` and `repeat` loosen a count. Regular expressions use the Rust dialect, with no lookaround or backreferences, and aren't anchored. The shape of one unit, such as a line or a frontmatter value, is exactly one of these: `text`, the text itself; `template`, the text with typed holes `${name:type}` where it varies, matched whole; or `pattern`, a regular expression. Every shape reads the unit's text squashed, with each run of whitespace read as one space. Each rule has an `example`, which is text of the kind that the rule requires. The engine checks the example against the rule, shows it with every failure that the rule raises, and writes it into the scaffold. The scaffold is the document that the schema derives and that a new document starts from. A rule that declares a template or a pattern must have an example. For what an example can't show, use `guidance`. The engine writes guidance into the scaffold before the part that it governs, and no failure prints it. In a markdown document, a unit is a heading, a paragraph, an item, a row, or a line of a fence. The body is the document's sections, in heading order, and the preamble before the first heading.

line-limit.description: The most lines that a document can have. A longer document is an error, and you split it. A value of zero or less sets no limit.

guidance.description: What the schema states that no example can show. The engine writes it into the scaffold after the sentence that every scaffold opens with. No failure prints it.

lifecycle.description: The states that the documents of the schema move through, with one entry per dimension, in order. Each dimension is a required frontmatter enum. Don't repeat it under `frontmatter`. A dimension is what `only` can name. The engine derives one scaffold for each combination of states.

frontmatter.description: The frontmatter keys, with one entry per key. A declared key is required unless it sets `optional`. The engine never rejects the keys that the host reserves. Declare a reserved key to require it or to narrow its value. An undeclared key that is neither reserved nor a lifecycle key is an error unless `frontmatter-open` is set.

frontmatter-open.description: Set to `true` to accept undeclared frontmatter keys. When absent, an undeclared key that isn't reserved or a lifecycle key is an error.

prohibited-patterns.description: Patterns that no body line may match, each with the message that states its rule. Fenced blocks, code spans, and the interiors of regions are excluded. A unit rule and a format take the same key, which then applies to the text that they govern instead.

formats.description: Line formats local to the schema, in the shape of the shared registry. The nearest layer wins: an entry here replaces an entry of the same name in a farther layer entirely.

types.description: Hole types local to the schema, in the shape of the shared registry. Each entry has a slug as its name and, as its value, either a regular expression with no anchor and no capture group or a list of literal choices. The nearest layer wins by name, and the engine compiles every format that the schema sees against the result. The built-in types are reserved: `text` (`.+`), `word`, `int`, `slug`, and `seq`.

examples.description: Complete documents that satisfy this schema. The engine checks each one as it checks any other document, at the states that its own frontmatter gives, so a marker in an example is an error. Examples show what a document of the type looks like, and the engine never copies them.

sections.description: The document's headings, in document order. A heading that no entry matches is an error unless an open region admits it. A heading more than one level deeper than the heading before it is an error. The engine reports an ordered schema whose entries skip a level on the schema.

sections-ordered.description: Set to `false` to accept the declared sections in any order. When absent, the sections must follow the listed order, and a section out of place is an error that names the first such heading.

sections-prohibited.description: Headings that are banned inside open regions.

block.description: One part of a body, read from the document's CommonMark blocks. Consecutive paragraphs form one prose block, and a paragraph of images only forms an image block. A block has a kind and units: the paragraphs of prose or a blockquote, the items of a list, the rows of a table, or the repetitions of a group. `each` applies one unit rule to every unit. `sequence` applies one rule per position and fixes the count. Otherwise, `min` and `max` bound the count. Generated blocks, region interiors, footnote definitions, and HTML comments are exempt from matching. Every rule reads the text with its generated anchors removed. The engine reports on the schema a key that doesn't apply to the block's kind.

kind.description: The kind of block. A `prose` block is paragraphs. A `bullet-list` or `numbered-list` block is items. A `table` block is a GFM table. A `code` block is a tagged fence. A `blockquote` block is quoted paragraphs. An `image` block is a paragraph of images only. An `html` block is an HTML block. A `thematic-break` block is a horizontal rule. A `references` block is link reference definitions outside the generated block. A `group` block is a repeating sequence of blocks.

optional.description: Set to `true` to let the block be absent. When absent, the block is required.

repeat.description: Set to `true` to let the block occur more than once in a row. When absent, it occurs once.

min.description: The minimum number of units. When absent, the minimum is one.

max.description: The maximum number of units. When absent, there is no upper bound.

sequence.description: One rule per unit, by position. The count is the length of the sequence unless an entry is optional or repeats. A unit must satisfy both `each` and the rule for its position.

rules.description: The grammar of the block's units, an alternative to `each` and `sequence`. An entry with a shape and no `select-pattern` is a production. A production takes the units that its shape matches, and each unit goes to the first such entry in order. An entry with a `select-pattern` takes the units that the guard selects and checks them. If it states only a guard and a count, it counts those units and takes nothing. An entry with neither takes every unit. `min` and `max` bound what each entry took or counted. A unit that no entry takes is an error unless `units-open` is set. The engine reports it against the production that it follows furthest.

units-open.description: Set to `true` to accept a unit that no entry of `rules` takes. When absent, such a unit is an error.

lang.description: The tag or tags that the fence must have, or `any`. A code block requires this key. An untagged fence is always an error. Applies to a block of kind code.

fence.description: The minimum number of backticks in the fence. When absent, the minimum is three. Applies to a block of kind code.

columns.description: The header row, in order. A table block requires this key. A differing header is an error. Applies to a block of kind table.

columns-open.description: Set to `true` to accept further columns after the declared ones. Applies to a block of kind table.

source-pattern.description: A regular expression that each image path must match. The engine matches an image in the host's reference scheme by what the host reports that it shows, and any other image as written. Applies to a block of kind image.

inline-html.description: Set to `true` to accept inline HTML in this block's units. When absent, any HTML other than a comment is an error.

blocks.description: The blocks of one repetition of the group. Applies to a block of kind group.

rule-id.description: The name by which other rules reference this block. Its keys are the keys that its units capture, except the keys of a unit rule that declares its own `rule-id`.

example.description: The text of one of this block's units, or a list of such texts. The engine uses it for every unit whose rule has no text or example of its own. A list gives those units in order, as the list of a unit rule does.

guidance.description: What an example can't show about this block. The engine writes it into the scaffold before the block.

severity.description: How the engine reports a failure of the rule: `error` reports an error, and `warn` reports a warning. A rule inside this one, such as a block's unit rule, takes this severity unless it declares its own. When absent, the rule takes the severity of the rule it sits in, and a failure of a rule in no other is an error.

example.description: One complete document that satisfies the schema at its own lifecycle states. The engine checks it as it checks any other document, and reports a marker in it on the schema.

format.description: One named line grammar, in a schema's `formats` or in a registry. A format has either one shape and its example, or `variants`, and each variant has a shape and an example. The engine shows an example beside every failure of its shape. An entry replaces the entry of the same name in a farther layer entirely, unless it declares `patch`.

else.description: One named line grammar, in a schema's `formats` or in a registry. A format has either one shape and its example, or `variants`, and each variant has a shape and an example. The engine shows an example beside every failure of its shape. An entry replaces the entry of the same name in a farther layer entirely, unless it declares `patch`.

patch.description: Set to `true` when this entry states only how it differs from the entry of the same name in a farther layer. The engine merges the two by JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386). A key stated here replaces the farther one, an omitted key is inherited, a key set to null is dropped, and a list replaces the farther list entirely. The keys below apply to the merged entry, so a patch contains only what it changes. The engine reports a patch that shadows no farther entry on the schema. When absent, the entry replaces the farther entry entirely.

text.description: The text that every bound line must equal.

template.description: The line written with typed holes where it varies, matched whole.

pattern.description: A regular expression that every bound line must match, for what a template can't express.

key.description: The hole or named group, present in every shape of the format, whose capture is the line's key.

variants.description: The named shapes of the format, in the order in which a line tries them. A line conforms when one of them matches. When none matches, the failure names the variant that the line follows furthest, the place where the line fails, and that variant's example. The example of each variant must match only its own variant.

prohibited-patterns.description: Patterns that no bound line may match, checked after the shape, each with its message.

example.description: One conforming line, for a format with one shape. In a format with variants, each variant has its own example.

format-variant.description: One named shape of a variant format.

text.description: The text that a line of this variant equals.

template.description: The line written with typed holes where it varies, matched whole.

pattern.description: A regular expression that a line of this variant matches.

example.description: One conforming line that matches only this variant.

frontmatter-constraint.description: What a schema can state about one frontmatter key. The key is required unless it sets `optional`.

template.description: The value written with typed holes where it varies, matched whole. On `id`, the template can contain only the holes that the engine fills in a new document. A `${:seq}` hole is unique within the kind, and the template can contain at most one. A `${:slug}` hole is one or more slug words. A `${<key>}` hole has no type and is named for a lifecycle key whose states are slugs. It contains the document's state for that key. Replacing each hole with `x` must yield a slug, and only `seq-width` can sit beside the template.

pattern.description: A regular expression that the value must match, for what a template can't express.

enum.description: The allowed values. The value must be one of them.

format.description: The format that the value must have. `url` requires an absolute URL. `slug` requires lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens.

seq-width.description: On `id`, the number of digits of the `seq` hole. When absent, the width is three.

list.description: Set to `true` when the value is a list. Then `const`, `pattern`, `enum`, and `format` apply to every element, and `min` and `max` bound the number of elements. A scalar where a list is declared, or a list where none is declared, is an error.

min.description: The minimum number of elements. When absent, there is no lower bound.

max.description: The maximum number of elements. When absent, there is no upper bound.

optional.description: Set to `true` to let the key be absent. When absent, the key is required.

only.description: Maps lifecycle dimensions to states, as on every rule that takes `only`.

example.description: The key's value, or one element of it when `list` is declared.

guidance.description: What an example can't show about this key. The engine writes it into the scaffold as a YAML comment line before the key.

severity.description: How the engine reports a failure of the rule: `error` reports an error, and `warn` reports a warning. A rule inside this one, such as a block's unit rule, takes this severity unless it declares its own. When absent, the rule takes the severity of the rule it sits in, and a failure of a rule in no other is an error.

heading.description: A section's heading as a unit rule. It defines the heading's shape, the key that it captures, and an example of the heading. A repeated section is cited by its key.

text.description: The exact heading text, or `{ from: <key> }` for the frontmatter value.

template.description: The heading written with typed holes where it varies, matched whole.

pattern.description: A regular expression that the heading must match, for what a template can't express. Write `^` and `$` to bind the ends.

key.description: The hole of the template, or the named group of the pattern, whose capture is the section's key.

unique.description: The scope within which the key is unique. When absent, the scope is `document`.

example.description: A heading of the kind that the template or the pattern requires.

key-derivation.description: Where the prefixes of a `key-derives-from` come from, and the separator that ends them.

rule.description: The rule whose keys are the allowed prefixes.

from.description: The frontmatter key whose value is the only allowed prefix.

separator.description: The literal text that ends the prefix. The engine splits the key at its first occurrence.

lifecycle-dimension.description: One ordered dimension of a lifecycle.

key.description: The frontmatter key that contains the state.

states.description: The states, in lifecycle order. The key's value must be one of them.

guidance.description: What the states mean. The engine writes it into the scaffold as a YAML comment line before the key.

preamble.description: The content before the first heading. A preamble has no heading, level, or repeat, only blocks.

blocks.description: The preamble's blocks, as for a section's `blocks`.

guidance.description: What an example can't show about the preamble. The engine writes it into the scaffold before the preamble.

severity.description: How the engine reports a failure of the rule: `error` reports an error, and `warn` reports a warning. A rule inside this one, such as a block's unit rule, takes this severity unless it declares its own. When absent, the rule takes the severity of the rule it sits in, and a failure of a rule in no other is an error.

prohibited-heading.description: One heading that is banned inside open regions.

severity.description: How the engine reports a failure of the rule: `error` reports an error, and `warn` reports a warning. A rule inside this one, such as a block's unit rule, takes this severity unless it declares its own. When absent, the rule takes the severity of the rule it sits in, and a failure of a rule in no other is an error.

prohibition.description: One banned pattern and the message that states its rule. A finding gives the message and the span that the pattern matched, and a scaffold writes the message after the guidance of the part that the pattern governs.

pattern.description: The regular expression that no governed text may match.

message.description: One sentence that states the rule as a fact about the part, in the voice of the document, such as "An interface's summary contains no modal verb."

section.description: One heading of the document. A section is required unless it sets `optional`, and occurs once unless it sets `repeat`. Its body runs to the next heading of any level. Nesting is by level, never by containment, except that a section that declares `parent` lies inside its parent. When an exact heading and a varying heading both match, the exact heading wins.

heading.description: The heading. It is the exact text, `{ from: <key> }` for the frontmatter value, or a `heading` rule for a heading that varies or captures a key. A string contains no hole. Write a heading that varies as a template, and give the template an example.

renamed-from.description: Former heading text, beside an exact heading. The engine reports a heading that has an old text, and its repair rewrites the heading.

rule-id.description: The name by which other rules reference this section. It must be unique within the schema.

optional.description: Set to `true` to let the section be absent. When absent, the section is required.

repeat.description: Set to `true` to let the heading occur more than once. When absent, it occurs once.

headings-open.description: Set to `true` to accept undeclared headings of this level or deeper after this section, up to the next declared heading. Only document-scope rules apply to their bodies, and `sections-prohibited` still applies.

subheadings-open.description: Set to `true` to act as `headings-open` does, but only for undeclared headings deeper than this level.

for-each-key-of.description: Requires one occurrence of this section for each key that the referenced rule captured, each key once. A list of rules pairs with the keys that any of them captured, and a key that two of them captured needs one occurrence. The engine reads the key of each occurrence by the heading's `key`, which the heading must declare. The referenced rule must capture a key. A missing occurrence and an orphan are each an error that names the key. Under a `parent`, the keys are those captured inside the same occurrence of the parent.

parent.description: The section that this one lies inside. The parent must have a smaller `level` and be listed before this section, with only its own subsections between them. Each occurrence must follow an occurrence of the parent, before the next heading of the parent's level or higher. `optional` and `repeat` count within each occurrence of the parent. A body still runs to the next heading.

number-from-parent.description: Set to `true` when the heading must begin with the number of its parent's heading, a dot, and a number, such as `4.2.1` under `4.2`. A number is the text before the first space: digits separated by dots. A parent heading with no number is an error.

blocks.description: The body, as an ordered list of blocks. When absent, the body is one prose block of one or more paragraphs. `[]` means an empty body. The body must be exactly these blocks, in order unless `blocks-ordered` is `false`.

blocks-ordered.description: Set to `false` to accept the declared blocks in any order. When absent, the blocks must appear in the declared order.

only.description: Maps lifecycle dimensions to states. The rule applies when the document's state is in the set for every dimension named. When absent, the rule always applies. The engine reports on the schema a dimension or state that the lifecycle doesn't declare, or `only` without a lifecycle.

guidance.description: What an example can't show about this section. The engine writes it into the scaffold before the section's heading.

examples.description: Further occurrences of a section that declares `repeat: true`. Each is the whole markdown text of one occurrence: a heading of the section's level, its body, and any sections inside it. The scaffold writes the occurrence that it derives from the rules, then each text, in order and unchanged. A section that declares `for-each-key-of` occurs once for each key of another rule: the scaffold writes the occurrence of the first key from the rules, the occurrence of each later key from the next text, and the occurrences that remain after the last text from the rules. The engine checks each text as part of the scaffold.

severity.description: How the engine reports a failure of the rule: `error` reports an error, and `warn` reports a warning. A rule inside this one, such as a block's unit rule, takes this severity unless it declares its own. When absent, the rule takes the severity of the rule it sits in, and a failure of a rule in no other is an error.

unit.description: A rule on one unit of a block: a paragraph, an item, a row, a line of a fence, or a repetition of a group. The engine matches a paragraph with its lines joined by one space, and a line of a fence without its indent. It matches an item's own text. Anything more that the item contains, such as a nested list or a fence, must match the rule's `blocks`. A rule has at most one shape: `text`, `template`, `pattern`, or the `format` that it binds.

text.description: The text that the unit must equal: a string, or `{ from: <key> }` for the frontmatter value. It applies to a paragraph, an item, or a line.

template.description: The unit's text written with typed holes where it varies, matched whole.

pattern.description: A regular expression that the unit's text must match, for what a template can't express. Write `^` and `$` to bind the ends.

format.description: The name of a line format that the unit's text must match.

key.description: The hole of the template, the named group of the pattern, or the hole or group of every shape of the format, whose capture is the unit's key. The key must be unique within its scope by its slug, and the slug names the key's generated anchor. Don't declare `key` beside a format that captures a key.

key-optional.description: Set to `true` to treat a unit that contains no key as plain rather than as an error. The key is the rule's own `key` or the one that its `format` declares. The engine reports a rule that has neither. When absent, a unit with no key is an error.

key-repeats.description: Set to `true` to let the rule capture one key on several units, and a key that another rule captures, as a list that names the owner of each item names one owner many times. Each capture by this rule refers to the key, which a capture by a rule without `key-repeats` defines where there is one. When absent, a second capture of a key is an error.

unique.description: The scope within which the key is unique. When absent, the scope is `document`. The engine reports a clash on both documents, and names the key and the other document.

rule-id.description: The name by which other rules reference this rule. The keys that it captures belong to it, not to the enclosing block.

for-each-key-of.description: Requires one unit that captures each key that the referenced rule captured, each key once, as a section's `for-each-key-of` pairs headings with keys. A list of rules pairs with the keys that any of them captured, each key once. This rule must capture a key, by `key` or by its format, and so must the referenced rule. A missing key and an orphan are each an error that names the key. When the section declares a `parent`, the keys are those captured inside the same occurrence of the parent. Otherwise, they are the keys of the document. The engine reports a missing key even where the block that would contain it is absent.

prohibited-patterns.description: Patterns that the unit's text must not match, each with its message.

optional.description: In a sequence, set to `true` to let this position be absent. When absent, the position is required.

repeat.description: In a sequence, set to `true` to let this position occur more than once. When absent, it occurs at most once.

blocks.description: The blocks that a list item contains beyond its own text. Each block is required in every item unless it sets `optional`. When absent, an item contains nothing beyond its text.

lines.description: The grammar of the content lines of a code or `html` block, as `rules` is the grammar of a block's units. Each line, without its indent, is a unit of its own. Blank lines don't count. A line that no rule takes is an error unless `lines-open` is set. A rule here can't contain `lines` or `blocks`. A key captured from a line belongs to the line rule's own `rule-id`, or else to the enclosing block's. A rule that contains `lines` can also state an `example`. That example is the whole fence: the scaffold copies it, and these rules read its keys out of it.

lines-open.description: Set to `true` to accept a line that no rule of `lines` takes. When absent, such a line is an error.

select-pattern.description: Under `rules` or `lines`, a regular expression that selects the units or lines that this rule governs by their text, for a rule that picks them by something other than its shape. A rule that states only a guard and a count counts what it matches and takes nothing.

min.description: Under `rules` or `lines`, the fewest units or lines that the rule may take or count. A rule that declares `select-pattern` must state `min`, because it has no default. Write `min: 0` to govern such units without requiring one. When absent on a rule without a guard, the minimum is one.

max.description: Under `rules` or `lines`, the most units or lines that the rule may take or count. When absent, there is no upper bound.

example.description: The text of a unit that this rule governs, or a list of such texts. A rule that binds a format and states no example of its own uses the format's example. The engine checks each text of a list against the rule, and a failure quotes the first. The scaffold writes one unit for each text of a list, in order, and copies of the last text while `min` demands more, but never more units than the `max` of the rule or of the block. A rule under `rules` writes its list even with `min: 0`. In a `sequence`, a position that declares `repeat` writes the whole list, and any other position writes the first text. In a `code` block, each text is one fence, so the block declares `repeat: true`.

severity.description: How the engine reports a failure of the rule: `error` reports an error, and `warn` reports a warning. A rule inside this one, such as a block's unit rule, takes this severity unless it declares its own. When absent, the rule takes the severity of the rule it sits in, and a failure of a rule in no other is an error.
